sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the sign-in page
sections.what: Brings in the form tools, the validation rules, the auth hook and the input and button parts.
sections.why: Standard setup. Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: LoginPage (part 1)
sections.title: Heading and social sign-in buttons
sections.what: Shows the page title and two buttons that start sign-in with Google or Apple. Both are disabled while sign-in is running.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives people a quicker sign-in choice. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The buttons only disable during loading, so the auth hook must report failures or the user gets no feedback.

sections.name: LoginPage (part 2)
sections.title: Email and password form
sections.what: Shows email and password fields with validation messages, a forgot-password link, a submit button that shows a spinner while working, and a link to create an account.
sections.why: Likely reason: standard sign-in. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The remember-me default is set but no checkbox appears here, so users cannot change it on this page.

summary: The sign-in page with Google and Apple buttons, plus an email and password form.
purpose: Lets a person log in to their Maate account.
why: Likely reason: social sign-in offers a faster route, and the email form covers everyone else. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Builds the form using the login validation rules. The social buttons start sign-in with a provider name. Submitting calls the login function. Links point to forgot-password and registration.
inputs: Email, password, and a remember-me default that has no visible checkbox.
outputs: Calls the login or social sign-in functions from the auth hook, which handle what happens next.
risks: Login errors are not displayed on this page. Display depends on the auth hook, which is not visible.
debug: If a button does nothing, check the auth hook and the login rules. If no error appears on failure, check the hook for error handling.
